definitions.explanation: Ill feeling or harmful intent toward others. Most often heard in the negative {邪気|じゃき}のない, meaning innocent, guileless, and free of any bad intentions.

definitions.gloss: evil energy; noxious influence; evil spirit
definitions.explanation: An unseen harmful force or malignant spirit, as imagined in folk belief. Something to be warded off or driven away for good health and fortune.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}には{邪気|じゃき}がない。
examples.english: That child has no malice; she is completely innocent.

examples.japanese: {邪気|じゃき}のない{笑顔|えがお}に{心|こころ}が{和|なご}んだ。
examples.english: His guileless smile put me at ease.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{冗談|じょうだん}には{邪気|じゃき}が{感|かん}じられず、みんなが{笑|わら}った。
examples.english: There was no malice in his joke, so everyone laughed.

examples.japanese: {節分|せつぶん}には{豆|まめ}をまいて{邪気|じゃき}を{追|お}い{払|はら}う。
examples.english: At Setsubun, people scatter beans to drive away evil spirits.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{人|ひと}は、{病気|びょうき}は{邪気|じゃき}によって{起|お}こると{考|かんが}えていた。
examples.english: People long ago believed that illness was caused by evil forces.

notes:
Two related senses: human ill will (sense 1) and unseen evil energy (sense 2). Sense 1 is by far the more common in everyday speech, almost always in {邪気|じゃき}のない.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {邪気|じゃき}のない: innocent; guileless
- {邪気|じゃき}を{払|はら}う: to ward off evil
- {邪気|じゃき}を{追|お}い{払|はら}う: to drive away evil spirits

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪意|あくい}: malice — the plain, everyday word for ill intent
- {無邪気|むじゃき}: innocent; naive — a common derived adjective built on {邪気|じゃき}
